title: Social Analytics Snapshot
description: DC-003-I028 — one immutable observation of one published social post at one point in time. Publisher Results (I025/I027) prove that publication occurred; a Social Analytics Snapshot records what happened after publication. Every collection produces a NEW snapshot — historical snapshots are never overwritten (see social-analytics-store.mjs, which has no replace()/update()). `provider` is deliberately a closed enum (Instagram/LinkedIn only, matching this milestone's own explicitly scoped platform list) rather than publisher-result.schema.json's free-form string — a future platform requires its own future milestone to extend this schema, mirroring control-centre.schema.json's own `by_provider` precedent. `status` is a fixed const, matching publisher-result.schema.json's own design: this schema represents a successful collection only — a failed collection attempt never produces a stored snapshot (see README "Failure Behaviour").

destination.description: The same safe account/author identifier already carried by the source Publisher Result's own `destination` field — an Instagram user ID or a LinkedIn `urn:li:person:...`/`urn:li:organization:...` author URN. Never a credential.

provider_post_reference.description: The platform post/media identifier this snapshot's metrics were collected for — copied verbatim from the source Publisher Result's own `provider_reference`. Never guessed or derived from a URL.

metrics.description: Provider-neutral map of metric name -> { value, availability }. Deliberately open (additionalProperties, no fixed required key set) — Instagram and LinkedIn expose different documented metric names for the content types I027 publishes, and this schema does not force either provider to supply a metric the other has. See README "Metric availability semantics" for the full per-provider list.

engagement.description: The one provider-independent engagement breakdown this milestone defines (brief §11): reactions, comments, shares, saves, each a normalized metricValue, plus a derived `total`. `total` is calculated ONLY when all four inputs are `available` — never a partial sum presented as complete, and never a guessed value when an input is unavailable.

source.description: `type: "mock"` honestly labels a snapshot collected via a mock adapter (mirrors execution_metadata.provider's own "templated-http" vs "mock-transport" real-vs-mock distinction elsewhere in this codebase) — `type: "provider-api"` is reserved for a genuine live collection, none of which have occurred as of this milestone's delivery (see README "Live-verification gates").

metricValue.description: A single normalized metric observation. Unavailable data is NEVER represented as a numeric zero (brief's own explicit rule) — `value` is `null` for every availability state except `available`, and a legitimate zero (e.g. zero comments) is only ever expressed as `{ value: 0, availability: "available" }`.

availability.description: available: a real numeric value was returned (may legitimately be 0). unavailable: the provider indicated this data could not be produced right now (e.g. Instagram's own documented "empty data set instead of 0" behavior). not-supported: this metric does not apply to this platform/content type at all (a client-side, pre-request classification, e.g. Instagram's per-media-type metric list). not-returned: the metric was requested but the provider's response simply omitted it, distinct from an explicit unavailable signal.
